Schizogamy, in turn, may be divided in two types; scissiparity where stolons are devel- oped from already existing segments, and gemmiparity where the stolon formation is achieved by newly added segments. Both types occur within Autolytinae and Syllinae. Reproduction takes place in the free water, either by broadcast spawning, or as in the nuptial dance of Autolytinae where the male stolon some swims around and entangles the female stolon with sperm in threads (Gidholm, 1965). blocks.text: There is evidence for direct sperm transfer with sper- matophores and even internal fertilization with male copulatory chaetae in several small, interstitial Syllidae (Franke, 1999; Kuper and Westheide, 1997a; b). Brooding is also common and vari- able. Epigamic Syllidae have direct development where the eggs and sometimes the larvae remain attached the female (in may to and Eusyllinae) (Figs. 11.1b, d). In schizogamic Syl- Exogoninae such Autolytus, the female stolons brood the larvae in lidae, as before dying. mode ventral egg sacs for some time An extreme is displayed by Syllis vivipara that broods the young in the coelom in the posterior part of the body. In due course, the juveniles emerge by breaking off from the posterior end. The endocrine control of Syllidae reproduction appears to involve prostomi- al stolon—or epigamy-promoting hormones and proventricular hormones that inhibit the sexual development (see Franke and Pfannenstiel (1984) and references within).
